quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the bump or pothole better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way to neutral first.
Accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Shift down one gear at a time. Release the clutch slowly between each downshift to help control your speed.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, when following another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Keep at least a four-second distance behind them.
Get as close to them as possible.
Not worry about your following distance.
Always ride on the left side of your lane so they can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least a four-second distance behind them.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least a four-second distance. Increase this distance if weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding next to another vehicle. The driver cannot see you there and may change lanes into you. Riding alongside also blocks your escape route if you need to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider?

options.text: One
Three to four
Six
More than eight

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do to ride safely at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when not near other vehicles, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead—their headlights and taillights help you see the road.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Shift gears while turning.
Shift gears before turning.
Change power suddenly while turning.
Use the brake the entire time in a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before turning.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn, not during the turn.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
Increases your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
Increases road hazards and lets others pass you easily.
Reduces road hazards and lets you follow closely behind vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
questions.explanation: The right lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route. Choose a position that increases your space cushion.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After riding for at least an hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their bike.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their bike.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space around your bike and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Always slow down.
Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
Speed up quickly.
Not worry about your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Rolling on the throttle through a turn stabilizes your bike's suspension. Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly as you go through the turn.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars seem:

options.text: Larger.
Farther away.
Faster.
Narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors, but they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Compared to riding during the day, a motorcycle rider at night should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Keep more space between their motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use their high beam whenever possible.
Follow other vehicles too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow other vehicles too closely.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk when riding at night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be flexible with your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign and proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward a little to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward a little to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, stop first where the sign indicates. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane begins. Lean your body forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to see if anything is coming. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you are looking.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while you are riding:

options.text: The steering will feel hard to turn.
The steering will feel loose.
The steering will feel the same.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel hard to turn.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel hard to turn. If your steering feels hard, exit the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the operator:

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals to show turns or stops. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means they plan to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you stay out of other drivers' blind spots.
Help you hide from other drivers.
Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you hide from other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, keeps you out of blind spots, avoids road hazards, protects your lane from other drivers, shows your intentions, helps you avoid wind blasts, and gives you an escape route from hazards.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show rules like speed limits are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid overworking them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight from a passenger in a sidecar changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need extra space to stop completely.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT needed for an eye or face shield to work well?

options.text: Free of scratches.
Resistant to penetration.
Able to fasten securely.
Airtight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight.
questions.explanation: Good eye protection and face shields must be free of scratches, resist penetration, give clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.question: What material is best for riding gloves?

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Polyester.
Silk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another tough material to protect your hands.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without one?

options.text: Stopping will be easier than when riding without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about as easy as it is when riding without the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to the motorcycle, which increases the braking power needed to stop. Stopping takes longer when going downhill and with added weight.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help prevent serious injury?

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet.
Face or eye protection.
Ear buds.
Protective clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.
